source: Owner-supplied research, 2026-11-21. Not verified by the lab: no upstream project was executed, pinned or benchmarked.

specimens.title: Fetch a page
specimens.question: Does "fetch this URL" describe one operation, or a chain of decisions?

anchor.note: Reference Fetch server: retrieves a page and converts HTML to Markdown. Documented to treat model-initiated tool calls and user-initiated prompts differently for robots.txt, and to check for non-public destinations.

diversions.note: Fork that removes robots.txt checking: similar capability, different policy.

specimens.bent: A published advisory describes a redirect leading to a disallowed destination without a second robots check. The current README describes per-hop checking. These are different revisions.
specimens.experiment: Serve an allowed page that redirects to a disallowed one. Compare final destination, returned content and recorded checks under each policy.

specimens.title: Memory
specimens.question: What actually remembers, and what decides which stored statement is true?

anchor.note: Reference server storing entities, observations and relations in a local knowledge graph. Its README warns the default storage location can sit in a package-managed directory.

diversions.note: Adds project/global database handling and a file marker against overwriting unrelated files.
Reimplements the graph-memory idea in Swift.
Applies the same graph concept to RPG worlds, organisations or reading notes.

specimens.bent: The interface promises memory, but persistence depends on where the file lives.
specimens.experiment: Store two facts about a fictional workshop. Restart the client, restart the server, change the storage path, then add a conflicting observation.

specimens.title: "Thinking" as a tool
specimens.question: Is this item recording thought, computing a plan, or consulting another intelligence?

anchor.note: Exposes a structured thinking process with revision and branching. The interface accepts thought text and sequence metadata from the caller.

specimens.bent: A tool with "thinking" in its name is not automatically another model.
specimens.experiment: Put three implementations behind similar icons: store caller-supplied steps, run a deterministic planner, ask another model. These are proposed lab implementations, not claims about the reference server.

specimens.title: Filesystem
specimens.question: Is the boundary defined at launch, by the client, or by the server's effective state?

anchor.note: File operations constrained by allowed directories given on the command line. For 2025-era clients, Roots sent by the client replace those directories unless --confine-roots is set. The README calls Roots deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28.

diversions.note: Issue 3602: CLI-provided directories versus client-provided Roots.

specimens.bent: Issue 3602 (roots replace command-line directories) was closed as working as designed. Issue 5094 (a roots update with no valid roots kept the previous list) is recorded as fixed; the current README describes revocation in that case.
specimens.experiment: Keep one launch directory. Let the client send a root outside it, a root containing it, a root inside it, then revoke. Compare three builds: roots replace, roots only narrow, and the build before the fix.
specimens.checked: README and issues 3602 and 5094 read on 2026-11-21 through a fetch tool. Not pinned to a commit; pull requests not opened.

specimens.title: Browser perception
specimens.question: Can the assistant not perform the action, or can it not perceive the target through this interface?

anchor.note: Interacts with pages through structured accessibility snapshots. Coordinate-based tools are opt-in through a vision capability.

diversions.note: Compare the structured snapshot with screenshots and visible page content.

specimens.bent: Release notes include fixes around snapshot content: the representation itself has edges.
specimens.experiment: A synthetic page with a labelled button, an unlabelled visual twin, a canvas and a control that changes after inspection.
specimens.checked: README read on 2026-11-21 through a fetch tool; the page was truncated, so tool descriptions rest on a summary. Not pinned.

specimens.title: CLI, reversed
specimens.question: Which parts discover a change dynamically, and which are generated artifacts that go stale?

anchor.note: An instrument for inspecting a server's capabilities and exchanges.

diversions.note: Calls servers from scripts and the terminal, and generates a standalone CLI from a server's tool definitions.

specimens.bent: The generator doc says an artifact embeds the resolved server definition and its metadata and "always targets that snapshot", and offers inspect-cli and generate-cli --from to refresh it. It does not settle whether tool schemas are fixed at generation time. The lab simulates the case where they are.
specimens.experiment: Generate a CLI, then change the server's schema.
specimens.checked: mcporter cli-generator doc and README read on 2026-11-21 through a fetch tool. Not pinned. The schema-snapshot question is not settled by those pages.

specimens.title: Local and remote
specimens.question: Who owns this server process, and whose state is it holding?

anchor.note: Runs stdio servers over SSE, WebSocket or Streamable HTTP. The README says each SSE and each WebSocket connection gets its own server process, and describes a stateful mode with a session timeout.

specimens.bent: Issue 35: one child process shared across SSE connections, so one client saw another’s state; the maintainer reports it fixed in v4.1.0, noting a reconnect gets a fresh child. Issue 126: a session-conflict error terminated the child on reconnect; reported fixed in v4.0.0. Issue 160: the session timeout never armed while a stream stayed open, leaking children after an ungraceful disconnect; reported fixed in v4.1.0 with pings.
specimens.experiment: Connect two clients to a specimen with explicit state. Disconnect one unexpectedly.
specimens.checked: supergateway README and issues 35, 126 and 160 read on 2026-11-21 through a fetch tool. Release notes not checked; not pinned.

specimens.title: The item becomes an application
specimens.question: Which participant knows the current state?

anchor.note: Interactive globe with geocoding; declares app resources and permitted external connections.

diversions.note: A later tool captures the current map view as a screenshot: human-visible state turned back into an artifact.

specimens.bent: The tool result, the displayed map and the model's information can all differ.
specimens.experiment: Let a person move the map, then compare the original tool result, the displayed map, a captured screenshot and what the model has.
specimens.checked: README of the map-server example read on 2026-11-21 (source files not read). It lists server tools geocode and show-map and app tools navigate-to, get-current-view and get-screenshot; it does not describe how a view changed by the person reaches the model, and shows no resource URI.

specimens.title: One item contains a language
specimens.question: Is the unit of responsibility a tool call, an individual effect, or the whole program?

anchor.note: Uses code execution to expose a broad API without sending its whole specification into the model's context.

diversions.note: Community demonstration converting MCP tools into TypeScript APIs. Experimental; not a performance validation.

specimens.bent: Batching does not give transaction semantics.
specimens.experiment: Run a batch as individual calls, then as one program. Fail after the second write.
specimens.checked: cloudflare/mcp README read on 2026-11-21. It describes search and execute tools where the model writes JavaScript run in isolated Workers, and a large token saving. It says nothing about partial failure or transactions.

specimens.title: Another intelligence
specimens.question: When did advice become delegated responsibility?

anchor.note: Exposes access to other LLMs: a direct model-as-capability example. Maintenance needs checking.

diversions.note: Composes models and MCP tools through routing, parallelism, orchestration and evaluation.

specimens.bent: A specialist cannot evaluate what it never receives.
specimens.experiment: Keep the expert fixed and change only the contract: answer a question, review an artifact, deliver a validated artifact. Then remove context from the handoff.
specimens.checked: sammcj/mcp-llm README read on 2026-11-21: tools generate_code, generate_code_to_file, generate_documentation, ask_question. Last commit date not visible. mcp-agent not read for this station.

specimens.title: Iteration and durable execution
specimens.question: Who says "good enough", what stops the loop, and which component supplies durability?

anchor.note: Evaluator-optimizer with quality evaluation and bounded refinement; examples include Temporal-backed execution.

diversions.note: Wrap a larger workflow inside the evaluator.

specimens.bent: A model rating is evidence of an assessment, not proof of correctness.
specimens.experiment: Set criteria that cannot all be satisfied. Interrupt execution and inspect what can resume.
specimens.checked: mcp-agent evaluator_optimizer.py and the Temporal example README read on 2026-11-21. The loop: minimum rating GOOD, at most 3 refinements, returns the best-rated response; the last refinement is never rated. The README credits Temporal with durability.

specimens.title: The network and the repair bench
specimens.question: Is one entrance also one domain, one authority, or one workflow?

anchor.note: Gateway describing aggregation, virtual servers and federation across capability sources.

diversions.note: Malformed and realistic inputs over actual transports.

specimens.bent: A scanner passing does not establish correctness. Use fuzzers only against authorised, isolated specimens.
specimens.experiment: Assemble one inventory from two backends, collide names, remove a dependency, change a schema.
specimens.checked: IBM/mcp-context-forge README read on 2026-11-21, truncated at about half. It describes a gateway, registry and proxy with federation and virtual servers. How tool-name collisions between backends are handled is not stated in what was read. Fuzzer repositories not read.

specimens.title: Inspect the inspector
specimens.question: What can be claimed about a server from what it says about itself, and on what grounds?

anchor.note: Reference tool for looking at what a server lists. The classification on this bench is this lab's own Lens proposal, not the Inspector's.

diversions.note: Owner-supplied note on recon tooling that enumerates and classifies a server's tool surface. Unverified.

specimens.bent: A profile built from a listing repeats the server's own words. Point the inspector at itself and the claim it most needs, that it is read-only, rests on its own declaration.
specimens.experiment: Profile a server, let its listing change after it was pinned, then have the inspector profile itself once.
